title: Neural Network Fundamentals
interviewAnswer: A neural network composes linear transformations with nonlinear activations. Training adjusts parameters to minimize a loss, while intermediate layers learn representations useful for the task.
why: Every DL interview expects you to explain a neural network from first principles, not just name PyTorch modules.
intuition: A neural network repeatedly performs weighted combinations followed by nonlinear transformations. Training adjusts the weights so those transformations produce useful representations for the task.
deepDive: A feed-forward layer computes z=Wx+b and activation a=φ(z). Stacking linear layers without nonlinearities collapses to one linear transformation, so activations create expressive nonlinear functions. The final layer/loss depends on the task: logits plus cross-entropy for classification, continuous outputs with regression losses, etc. Parameters are learned by backpropagation and an optimizer over mini-batches.
workedExample: For image classification, early layers may detect local edges/textures while later layers combine them into task-specific patterns before the classifier head.
code:
import torch.nn as nn
model=nn.Sequential(
  nn.Linear(20,64), nn.ReLU(),
  nn.Linear(64,1)
)
commonMistakes: Saying neurons “think” independently rather than describing tensor operations.
Forgetting that outputs are usually logits before softmax/sigmoid loss handling.
Assuming more layers always improve performance.
followUps: Why do we need nonlinear activations?
How do you choose output activation/loss?
What causes overfitting in neural networks?
production: The architecture is only one part of a DL system; reproducible preprocessing, checkpoints, device/mixed-precision handling and monitoring are equally important.

lab.goal: Train a tiny MLP end-to-end and inspect gradients.
lab.buildIt:
import torch
x=torch.linspace(-2,2,200).unsqueeze(1); y=(x**2)
model=torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(1,32),torch.nn.ReLU(),torch.nn.Linear(32,1))
opt=torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(),lr=1e-2)
for _ in range(500):
    opt.zero_grad(); loss=torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(model(x),y); loss.backward(); opt.step()
print('loss',loss.item())
lab.useIt:
# Same pattern scales to real tasks: Dataset/DataLoader -> nn.Module -> loss -> optimizer.
print(model(torch.tensor([[1.5]])).item())
lab.verifyIt:
assert loss.item()<0.02
assert all(p.grad is not None for p in model.parameters())
